boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Smith College
boards.description: Current, under-21-safe food and essentials destinations with official late-hour evidence in Northampton and nearby Hadley/Holyoke.

cards.title: Amanouz Café
cards.subtitle: 44 Main St, Northampton
cards.notes: Use the official hours before heading downtown; the café lists service through 10 p.m. most nights and 11 p.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A downtown Moroccan and Mediterranean option with posted late-evening hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Amanouz Café lists hours until 10 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and until 11 p.m. Friday–Saturday at 44 Main Street.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists 8 a.m.–10 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and 8 a.m.–11 p.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Teapot
cards.subtitle: 116 Main St, Northampton
cards.notes: Check the day’s posted schedule, then use its Main Street location for takeout or delivery; vegetarian dishes are listed on the official site.
cards.short_summary: Chinese restaurant and delivery option with late posted closing times.
cards.evidence_claim: Teapot lists hours until 10 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and until 11 p.m. Friday–Saturday at 116 Main Street.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists 11 a.m.–10 p.m. Monday–Thursday, 11 a.m.–11 p.m. Friday–Saturday, and 11:30 a.m.–10 p.m. Sunday.

cards.title: Joe's Cafe
cards.subtitle: 33 Market St, Northampton
cards.notes: Plan for an earlier late-evening stop: the restaurant lists a 10 p.m. close, with its kitchen closing at 9:30 p.m.
cards.short_summary: A Market Street pizza-and-spaghetti restaurant with a defined kitchen cutoff.
cards.evidence_claim: Joe's Cafe lists Monday–Saturday hours from 4–10 p.m., with the kitchen closing at 9:30 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Monday–Saturday 4–10 p.m.; kitchen closes at 9:30 p.m.; closed Sunday.

cards.title: Domino's Pizza
cards.subtitle: 241 King St, Northampton
cards.notes: Use the location’s ordering page to confirm availability before leaving; it identifies this Northampton store and supports carryout or delivery orders.
cards.short_summary: A King Street pizza location with an official store-specific order page.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino's official page identifies its Northampton store at 241 King Street Suite 115 and offers takeout or delivery ordering.
cards.source_title: Domino's Pizza at 241 King Street Suite 115
cards.access_notes: The official store page directs visitors to its current Hours section and states that location hours vary; verify the live close time before departing.

cards.title: Taco Bell on King Street
cards.subtitle: 203 King St, Northampton
cards.notes: This is the longest-hours option in Northampton proper. Confirm whether you want dine-in, drive-thru, delivery, or takeout before going.
cards.short_summary: A Northampton fast-food location whose official page publishes overnight hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists its 203 King Street Northampton location with drive-thru hours until 3 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 5 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists drive-thru and dine-in hours until 3 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 5 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.

cards.title: Stop & Shop on King Street
cards.subtitle: 228 King St, Northampton
cards.notes: For groceries or prepared-food ingredients, use the store’s official listing and arrive before the posted close; Sunday has the earlier closing time.
cards.short_summary: A full grocery-store option open into the evening.
cards.evidence_claim: Stop & Shop lists its 228 King Street store open until 10 p.m. Monday–Saturday and until 9 p.m. Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Official listing gives store hours of 7 a.m.–10 p.m. Monday–Saturday and 7 a.m.–9 p.m. Sunday.

cards.title: Taco Bell in Hadley
cards.subtitle: 348 Russell St, Hadley
cards.notes: If you are already traveling along Route 9, check the official location page for live availability and use its stated drive-thru hours.
cards.short_summary: A nearby Hadley location with published overnight drive-thru service.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists its 348 Russell Street Hadley location with drive-thru hours until 2 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 3 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists drive-thru hours until 2 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 3 a.m. Thursday–Saturday; dine-in closes earlier.

cards.title: Taco Bell in Holyoke
cards.subtitle: 2199 Northampton St, Holyoke
cards.notes: Use this farther option only when you have a safe ride arranged; the official page separates late drive-thru access from earlier dine-in service.
cards.short_summary: A Holyoke location with a late drive-thru schedule published by the restaurant.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists its 2199 Northampton Street Holyoke location with drive-thru hours until 2 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists drive-thru until 2 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3 a.m. Friday–Saturday; dine-in hours end earlier.

cards.title: Packard's Kitchen
cards.subtitle: 14 Masonic St, Northampton
cards.notes: Use the restaurant kitchen hours, not the later venue closing time, when planning a food order; its official page lists kitchen cutoffs by day.
cards.short_summary: A downtown kitchen with posted food service as late as 11 p.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Packard's lists kitchen service until 10 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and until 11 p.m. Friday–Saturday at 14 Masonic Street.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists kitchen until 10 p.m. Monday–Thursday and Sunday, and until 11 p.m. Friday–Saturday. Food access is not restricted to patrons 21+.

cards.title: Campus Pizza
cards.subtitle: 150 Fearing St, Amherst
cards.notes: For a late weekend order in Amherst, use the restaurant’s official schedule and confirm a safe round-trip plan before traveling from Smith.
cards.short_summary: An Amherst pizza counter with explicitly posted late weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Pizza lists Thursday–Saturday hours from 5 p.m.–2 a.m. at 150 Fearing Street in Amherst.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Thursday–Saturday 5 p.m.–2 a.m.; Wednesday 5–10 p.m.; Sunday 4–9 p.m.; closed Monday–Tuesday.

warnings: Late availability can change for holidays, special events, and operational needs; confirm the official source before leaving. Two farther options are included only for students with safe transportation.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Smith spaces for studying, gathering, making, viewing art, and spending time outdoors.

cards.title: Julia McWilliams Child ’34 Campus Center
cards.subtitle: Central gathering and meeting space
cards.notes: Use the skylit main-level concourse to sit, study, eat, or talk; check whether your group needs to reserve a room before planning a gathering.
cards.short_summary: A central campus building with informal seating and reservable group spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith says the main-level concourse is a place to sit, study, eat and converse, while the upper level includes spaces for groups and student organizations.
cards.source_title: Office of Student Engagement — Julia McWilliams Child ’34 Campus Center
cards.access_notes: After 6 p.m. during the academic year, access is restricted to active Smith community members using an active OneCard.

cards.title: Goldstein Lounge
cards.subtitle: Campus Center lounge for reading or working together
cards.notes: Bring a book or meet a classmate in the lounge; choose another space if it is being used for an official campus activity.
cards.short_summary: A lounge in the Campus Center intended for relaxing, reading, and studying with friends.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith identifies Goldstein Lounge as a space for relaxing, studying with friends, or reading in a wing-back chair.
cards.source_title: Office of Student Engagement — Julia McWilliams Child ’34 Campus Center
cards.access_notes: Located on the Campus Center main level; Campus Center access is OneCard-restricted after 6 p.m. during the academic year.

cards.title: Neilson Library
cards.subtitle: Multi-floor study, research, and collaboration building
cards.notes: Pick a carrel, table, soft seat, or group room based on the kind of work you need; use the library’s reservation information for bookable spaces.
cards.short_summary: Smith’s library provides varied individual and group study settings across its floors.
cards.evidence_claim: Neilson Library lists soft seating, study carrels, tables, group study rooms, quiet zones, and reservable spaces.
cards.access_notes: Use the library’s current space and reservation guidance; some spaces are designated quiet.

cards.title: Skyline Reading Room and Terrace
cards.subtitle: Fourth-floor Neilson Library reading space
cards.notes: Set up for a reading or writing session in the fourth-floor room, then use the terrace only when it is open and weather conditions allow.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor reading room paired with a seasonal terrace.
cards.evidence_claim: Neilson Library identifies the Skyline Reading Room and Terrace on its fourth floor and notes that the terrace closes at 6 p.m. in warm weather and over winter.
cards.access_notes: Terrace closes at 6 p.m. during warm weather and is closed over winter; confirm current library access before visiting.

cards.title: Klingenstein Browsing Room
cards.subtitle: Neilson Library room used for scheduled gatherings
cards.notes: Check the current schedule before relying on this room for a group meet-up, and select another library study area if a class or event has it booked.
cards.short_summary: A named Neilson Library room that appears in Smith’s classroom and event-space listings.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith lists the Klingenstein Browsing Room among Neilson Library’s reservable lecture and social-gathering spaces.
cards.access_notes: Availability is schedule-dependent; Smith directs space requests and scheduling through 25Live.

cards.title: Lyman Plant House & Conservatory
cards.subtitle: Botanic Garden conservatory and exhibit space
cards.notes: Plan a daylight visit to see the conservatory and its exhibits; consult the garden page before going because holiday and flower-show closures can apply.
cards.short_summary: A public, indoor Botanic Garden destination with permanent and temporary exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: The Botanic Garden says Lyman Plant House & Conservatory is free and open to the public, with exhibits throughout the building.
cards.source_title: Visit the Botanic Garden of Smith College
cards.access_notes: Listed daily 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; closed during the Smith College winter break and on specified holidays, with possible flower-show changes.

cards.title: Campus Arboretum and Gardens
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Botanic Garden landscapes across campus
cards.notes: Use a walk between classes to explore the managed gardens and arboretum; stay on established paths and review group-tour guidance for larger visits.
cards.short_summary: Smith’s outdoor garden and arboretum landscapes are open throughout the year.
cards.evidence_claim: The Botanic Garden describes a 127-acre arboretum and six acres of managed outdoor gardens, and states that the Campus Arboretum and Gardens are open daily to the public year-round.
cards.source_title: Visit the Botanic Garden of Smith College
cards.access_notes: Open daily to the public year-round; groups of 10 or more should schedule an unguided or guided visit in advance.

cards.title: Smith College Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: Four floors of collection and exhibition galleries
cards.notes: Choose an exhibition or collection gallery for a short art break, and use the museum’s visit page to confirm the day’s hours before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A free campus art museum with collection galleries and public programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum states that it is free and open to all, with collection galleries and a calendar of talks, workshops, and other programs.
cards.source_title: Visit | Smith College Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Museum hours are posted on its visit page; it is closed Mondays and major holidays.

cards.title: Hillyer Jannotta Student Gallery
cards.subtitle: Student and faculty art exhibition space in Hillyer Hall
cards.notes: Stop by when you are already near Hillyer to view the rotating work, then check current exhibition information before making a special trip.
cards.short_summary: A named Hillyer Hall gallery for rotating student and faculty art displays.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith’s Imaging Center identifies Hillyer Jannotta Student Gallery as a site for rotating exhibits of art department student and faculty work.
cards.access_notes: Located on the third floor of Hillyer Hall; confirm current building and exhibition access before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Mendenhall Center for the Performing Arts
cards.title: Mendenhall Center for the Performing Arts
cards.subtitle: Theatre, dance, rehearsal, and performing-arts library hub
cards.notes: Look for a scheduled theatre or dance event, or visit the building for its named performance and learning spaces; check ticket details for each production.
cards.short_summary: A Green Street performing-arts center with stages, studios, and the Josten Performing Arts Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith says Mendenhall houses dance studios, classrooms, production labs, the Werner Josten Performing Arts Library, and Theatre 14.
cards.access_notes: Performance access and ticketing vary by event; SmithArts lists Theatre 14 at 122 Green Street and box-office information.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-admission activities at Smith and nearby Northampton, each supported by a direct public-access or free-admission source.

cards.title: Wander the Lyman Plant House
cards.subtitle: Botanic Garden of Smith College
cards.notes: Walk the conservatory’s plant collections at your own pace, then use the garden’s visit page to confirm the day’s access before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A free indoor plant stop on the Smith campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith’s Botanic Garden says it is free and open to the public year-round and lists the Lyman Plant House & Conservatory among its visitable collections.
cards.source_title: Visit the Botanic Garden of Smith College
cards.access_notes: Listed daily 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; closed during the college winter break and on listed holiday closures. Check the official page for changes.

cards.title: Take an arboretum walk
cards.subtitle: Botanic Garden of Smith College
cards.notes: Choose a short loop through the campus trees and pause to look closely at seasonal changes; it works well as a low-key walk with a friend.
cards.short_summary: A free, year-round walk through Smith’s tree collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith’s Botanic Garden states that visitors can explore its 127-acre arboretum and that the garden is free and open to the public year-round.
cards.source_title: Visit the Botanic Garden of Smith College
cards.access_notes: The official visit page lists the Campus Arboretum and Gardens as open daily to the public year-round.

cards.title: Sit by Capen Garden’s fountain
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Gardens, Botanic Garden of Smith College
cards.notes: Use the fountain and perennial border as a conversation stop, then take a slow lap around the rose arbor and surrounding beds.
cards.short_summary: A fountain-centered outdoor garden on the Smith campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith identifies Capen Garden as an outdoor garden with a small fountain, perennial border, rose arbor, gazebo, and surrounding beds; the Botanic Garden is free and open to the public year-round.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Gardens: Capen, Happy Chace, Systematics, Rock, Perennial Border, Wilson Bulb Bank, Trudy's
cards.access_notes: Outdoor gardens are part of Smith’s Botanic Garden; its official visit page says the garden is free and open to the public year-round.

cards.title: Follow the paths at Happy Chace
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Gardens, Botanic Garden of Smith College
cards.notes: Meet behind the President’s House and follow the fragrant paths to the open-air pavilion, taking in the view toward Paradise Pond and the Mill River.
cards.short_summary: A terraced garden overlooking Paradise Pond.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith describes the Happy Chace 1928 Garden as a terraced garden behind the President’s House with fragrant pathways, an open-air pavilion, and views of Paradise Pond and the Mill River.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Gardens: Capen, Happy Chace, Systematics, Rock, Perennial Border, Wilson Bulb Bank, Trudy's
cards.access_notes: Outdoor gardens are within the Botanic Garden, which Smith says is free and open to the public year-round.

cards.title: Take the Japanese Garden path
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Gardens, Botanic Garden of Smith College
cards.notes: Walk the wooded hillside route beside Paradise Pond, moving slowly enough to notice how the garden’s features sit within the New England landscape.
cards.short_summary: A wooded hillside garden beside Paradise Pond.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith says the Japanese Garden is on the wooded hillside beside Paradise Pond and was built to demonstrate harmony with nature and offer space for contemplation and reflection.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Gardens: Capen, Happy Chace, Systematics, Rock, Perennial Border, Wilson Bulb Bank, Trudy's
cards.access_notes: Outdoor gardens are within the Botanic Garden, which Smith says is free and open to the public year-round.

cards.title: Compare blooms in the Systematics Garden
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Gardens, Botanic Garden of Smith College
cards.notes: Bring a friend and compare flower shapes across the beds; the planting arrangement is designed around evolutionary relationships among the species.
cards.short_summary: A garden arranged to show relationships among flowering plants.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith says the Systematics Garden arranges diverse flowering species in beds that reflect current scientific understanding of their evolutionary relationships.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Gardens: Capen, Happy Chace, Systematics, Rock, Perennial Border, Wilson Bulb Bank, Trudy's
cards.access_notes: Outdoor gardens are within the Botanic Garden, which Smith says is free and open to the public year-round.

cards.title: Browse the SCMA galleries
cards.subtitle: 20 Elm Street, Smith College
cards.notes: Pick one floor or exhibition to explore together, then pause with a single work and trade observations before moving on through the galleries.
cards.short_summary: Free public access to Smith’s art museum galleries.
cards.evidence_claim: The Smith College Museum of Art states that it is free and open to all.
cards.source_title: Accessing the Collection | Smith College Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: The museum says its galleries are closed to the public on Mondays; check the museum’s visit information before going.

cards.title: Catch a Music Department performance
cards.subtitle: Smith College performing-arts venues
cards.notes: Check the department calendar, choose a program that fits your evening, and arrive a little early to settle in before the performance begins.
cards.short_summary: Public Smith music events require neither admission nor reservation.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith College states that all Music Department events are free and open to the public, with no tickets or reservations required.
cards.source_title: Attend an Event for Smith College Performing Arts
cards.access_notes: Confirm the event date, venue, and program on Smith’s calendar. The page notes that Valley Classical Concert series events are an exception and require tickets.

cards.title: Meet on the Hess Stage lawn
cards.subtitle: Forbes Library, 20 West Street, Northampton
cards.notes: Bring a conversation or a book and use the open lawn around the stage as a daylight meet-up; leave the space ready for the next visitors.
cards.short_summary: A free outdoor gathering spot at Northampton’s public library.
cards.evidence_claim: Forbes Library states that the Hess Performance Stage and library grounds are free and open to the public during daylight hours when not in use by library programming.
cards.source_title: Grand Opening of New Stage – Forbes Library
cards.access_notes: Free public access is during daylight hours when the stage and grounds are not being used by library programming.

cards.entity_name: Forbes Library Neighborhood Free Book Boxes
cards.title: Choose a free book to keep
cards.subtitle: Northampton, Florence, and Leeds locations
cards.notes: Find a box on your route, browse the replenished selection, and take a book that catches your attention for a no-cost reading break.
cards.short_summary: Library-supported neighborhood boxes stocked with free books.
cards.evidence_claim: Forbes Library says its Neighborhood Free Book Boxes give children, teens, and adults access to free books and are replenished weekly by staff and volunteers.
cards.source_title: Neighborhood Free Book Boxes – Forbes Library
cards.access_notes: Boxes are located throughout Northampton, Leeds, and Florence; use the library’s information to identify a convenient box.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct, documented Smith College library study environments in Northampton.

cards.title: Neilson 302 Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Neilson Library, third floor
cards.notes: Bring reading or writing that benefits from a dedicated reading-room setting; the library lists this room among individual and large-table study options.
cards.short_summary: A named third-floor reading room with individual and group-study furnishings.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith Libraries lists Neilson 302 Reading Room as an individual study space and among locations with large study tables.
cards.access_notes: Most study spaces on the Libraries page are first-come, first-served; check current Neilson Library hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Neilson 401 Skyline Reading Room and Terrace
cards.title: Neilson 401 Skyline Reading Room and Terrace
cards.subtitle: Neilson Library, fourth floor
cards.notes: Set up at the reading-room tables, then use the terrace only when it is open; Smith notes seasonal and evening terrace closures.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor reading room paired with a seasonal outdoor terrace.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith Libraries identifies the fourth-floor Skyline Reading Room and Terrace as both an individual study space and a large-table study location.
cards.access_notes: The terrace closes at 6 p.m. during warm weather and is closed over winter; library hours apply.

cards.title: Neilson 015 Ground Floor Stacks Carrels
cards.subtitle: Neilson Library, ground floor
cards.notes: Choose a carrel for quiet individual work and keep conversation brief; it is one of the library’s designated quiet-study locations.
cards.short_summary: Quiet carrels located in Neilson’s ground-floor stacks.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith Libraries designates the ground-floor stacks carrels in Neilson 015 as a quiet study space.
cards.access_notes: Designated quiet study; individual library carrels generally cannot be reserved.

cards.title: Neilson 210 North Wing Study Area
cards.subtitle: Neilson Library, second-floor north wing
cards.notes: Use this designated quiet area for concentrated reading or laptop work; select a carrel or table and keep sound low.
cards.short_summary: A quiet second-floor north-wing study area with carrels and tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith Libraries lists Neilson 210, the second-floor north-wing study area, as a quiet study space.
cards.access_notes: Designated quiet study; check Neilson Library’s current open hours before going.

cards.title: Neilson 310 North Wing Study Area
cards.subtitle: Neilson Library, third-floor north wing
cards.notes: Head upstairs for a designated quiet-study area with a choice of study carrels and larger tables for independent work.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor quiet-study area with carrels and larger worktables.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith Libraries lists Neilson 310, the third-floor north-wing study area, as quiet study and as a location with large study tables.
cards.access_notes: Designated quiet study; individual library carrels generally cannot be reserved.

cards.title: Neilson 102 Browsing Room
cards.subtitle: Neilson Library, first floor
cards.notes: Use the large tables for a shared work session, and confirm the room is not assigned before relying on it for a longer block.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor browsing room documented with large study tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith Libraries lists Neilson 102 Browsing Room among locations with large study tables and identifies it as a Neilson Library space.
cards.access_notes: The room is also used for teaching and events; contact the Registrar’s Office for scheduled use.

cards.title: Neilson 108 Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: Neilson Library, first floor
cards.notes: Pair your study session with scheduled peer support, workshops, or a study group; tutors and partner programs work from this student-centered space.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor collaborative learning space with peer academic support.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith identifies the Learning Commons in Neilson 108 as a student-centered space for collaborative learning, tutoring, workshops, and study groups.
cards.access_notes: Open during all Neilson Library open hours; tutoring and programs occur throughout the semester.

cards.title: Hillyer Art Library Second Floor
cards.subtitle: Hillyer Art Library
cards.notes: Use the second floor when you need a designated quiet setting, especially for reading, writing, or reviewing visual-arts materials.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet-study floor within Smith’s art library.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith Libraries lists the second floor of Hillyer Art Library as a quiet study space.
cards.access_notes: Hillyer has variable noise levels outside its listed quiet-study area; check current library hours.

cards.title: Josten J133 Listening Room
cards.subtitle: Josten Performing Arts Library
cards.notes: For a small shared work session, use the room when it is not otherwise in use; check with Josten staff if you need to reserve it.
cards.short_summary: A performing-arts library listening room with large tables when unbooked.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith Libraries lists Josten J133 Listening Room as a large-table group-study location when it is not otherwise in use.
cards.access_notes: Open for use when not reserved; contact Josten Library for reservation details and current access.

cards.entity_name: Alumnae Gymnasium Third Floor Study Area
cards.title: Alumnae Gymnasium Third Floor Study Area
cards.subtitle: Alumnae Gymnasium, third floor
cards.notes: Use the third-floor soft seating and large tables for individual or group work; bring your Smith OneCard for round-the-clock swipe access.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour study area with soft seating and large tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith Libraries lists the Alumnae Gymnasium third floor for soft seating and large-table study, and states that Alumnae Gymnasium is open 24 hours for study.
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours for study; Smith Libraries describes the building as having 24-hour swipe access.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on off-campus Northampton corridors, each with a directly sourced reason to stop.

cards.title: Pulaski Park
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 240 Main St.
cards.notes: Use the Main Street park’s benches, chairs, tables, playground, or performance space for a short outdoor stop.
cards.short_summary: A city park with several documented public-use features.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists Pulaski Park at 240 Main Street with benches, chairs, tables, a playground, and performance space.
cards.access_notes: Located in downtown Northampton; check city programming separately.

cards.title: Academy of Music Theatre
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 274 Main St.
cards.notes: Check the theatre’s program, then use its Main Street entrance beside Pulaski Park when a performance fits your plans.
cards.short_summary: A downtown performance venue at the Main and New South Street corner.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academy of Music Theatre is at 274 Main Street, at the corner of Main and New South streets.
cards.source_title: Map and Directions | Academy of Music
cards.access_notes: The theatre directs visitors to its box office for ticket reservations; performance availability varies.

cards.title: Thornes Marketplace
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 150 Main St.
cards.notes: Walk through the marketplace’s levels and use its directory to choose a shop, restaurant, or experience before visiting.
cards.short_summary: A historic downtown marketplace with shops, eateries, and experiences.
cards.evidence_claim: Thornes identifies itself as a historic downtown marketplace at 150 Main Street with more than 25 local shops, eateries, and experiences.
cards.access_notes: Regular marketplace hours and individual tenant hours differ; check the directory before going.

cards.title: R. Michelson Galleries
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor — 132 Main St.
cards.notes: Plan a gallery visit around the posted hours and spend time with the fine-art and illustration work on view.
cards.short_summary: A Main Street gallery presenting fine art and children’s-book illustration.
cards.evidence_claim: R. Michelson Galleries lists its fine-art gallery at 132 Main Street and identifies fine art and illustration among its offerings.
cards.access_notes: Posted gallery hours vary by day; confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Forbes Library
cards.subtitle: West Street corridor — 20 West St.
cards.notes: Use the public library’s collections or local-history resources, and reserve archival research in advance if that is your goal.
cards.short_summary: Northampton’s public library, with local-history and special-collections resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Forbes Library is located at 20 West Street and lists local history, special collections, and the Calvin Coolidge Presidential Library and Museum among its resources.
cards.access_notes: Library hours are posted separately; archival research appointments are recommended.

cards.title: Historic Northampton
cards.subtitle: Bridge Street corridor — 46 Bridge St.
cards.notes: Visit the Main Gallery on Bridge Street to engage with an exhibition, then allow time to look at the historic campus grounds.
cards.short_summary: A local-history museum and gallery on the Route 9 approach to downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Northampton’s Main Gallery is at 46 Bridge Street, and its current exhibition is listed with admission by donation.
cards.access_notes: The site lists gallery hours Wednesday through Sunday, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m.; verify before travel.

cards.title: 33 Hawley
cards.subtitle: Hawley Street corridor — 33 Hawley St.
cards.notes: Review the resident organizations’ calendars and visit this accessible arts building for a class, workshop, rehearsal, or performance.
cards.short_summary: A shared community-arts building stewarded by three local arts organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: 33 Hawley at 33 Hawley Street is stewarded by Northampton Center for the Arts, A.P.E., and Northampton Open Media, each with programming there.
cards.source_title: 33 Hawley — Northampton Center for the Arts
cards.access_notes: The building lists Wednesday–Saturday open hours; individual events and rentals have separate arrangements.

cards.title: Northampton Community Music Center
cards.subtitle: South Street corridor — 139 South St.
cards.notes: Look for a public performance or activity at the music center, whose programs combine education, performances, and community access.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit community music organization on South Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Northampton Community Music Center is a nonprofit at 139 South Street whose mission includes music education, performances, and accessible activities.
cards.access_notes: Check the center’s current calendar or contact it for program-specific attendance details.

cards.title: Northampton Station
cards.subtitle: Pleasant Street corridor — 170 Pleasant St.
cards.notes: Use the station as a Pleasant Street transit landmark and confirm your train’s schedule, platform guidance, and ticket requirements beforehand.
cards.short_summary: An Amtrak station within walking distance of Main Street and Smith College.
cards.evidence_claim: Amtrak’s Great American Stations page lists Northampton station at 170 Pleasant Street and notes walking access to Main Street and Smith College.
cards.access_notes: Consult Amtrak for current schedules, service notices, and boarding information.

cards.title: Frank Newhall Look Memorial Park
cards.subtitle: North Main Street corridor — 300 North Main St., Florence
cards.notes: Use the North Main Street park as a destination for its listed outdoor facilities, and check the park’s rules before planning an activity.
cards.short_summary: A Florence park with courts, picnic areas, a theater, and other named facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Frank Newhall Look Memorial Park lists its address as 300 North Main Street and identifies facilities including tennis courts, picnic sites, Pines Theater, and a gazebo.
cards.source_title: Frank Newhall Look Memorial Park: Facilities
cards.access_notes: Confirm park access, facility availability, and any activity-specific requirements with the park.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Smith College rituals that mark the academic year, community gatherings and commencement.

cards.title: Begin the year in John M. Greene Hall
cards.subtitle: Formal opening of the college year
cards.notes: Look for the opening address and Glee Club performance held for entering students and faculty before classes begin.
cards.short_summary: Smith’s formal first gathering of the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith identifies President’s Welcome Assembly as the formal beginning of the college year, with first-year students, faculty, an opening address and Glee Club performance.
cards.access_notes: Program details are announced by Smith for each academic year.

cards.title: Wait for the bells to declare a fall holiday
cards.subtitle: Surprise autumn break from classes
cards.notes: Listen for the college bells on a fall day; Smith’s president announces the surprise break, then students choose their own daytime plans.
cards.short_summary: A bell-signaled fall holiday that dates to 1877.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith says Mountain Day is a surprise break from classes announced by the president ringing the college bells; the first was held in 1877.
cards.access_notes: The date is not fixed; Smith announces it on a suitable fall day.

cards.title: Attend the Cromwell Day program
cards.subtitle: Annual programs honoring Otelia and Adelaide Cromwell
cards.notes: Check Smith’s annual schedule for workshops, lectures, films and entertainment honoring Otelia Cromwell and Adelaide Cromwell.
cards.short_summary: A campus-wide day of learning and reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith describes Cromwell Day as an annual slate of workshops, lectures, films and entertainment honoring Otelia Cromwell, class of 1900, and Adelaide Cromwell ’40.
cards.access_notes: Morning and afternoon classes are canceled so students can attend the scheduled events.

cards.title: Find Julia Child Day at dinner
cards.subtitle: Thursday before Thanksgiving
cards.notes: Visit a campus dining hall on the Thursday before Thanksgiving to see the annual dinner honoring alumna Julia McWilliams Child ’34.
cards.short_summary: A dining tradition celebrating Smith’s famed cookbook-author alumna.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith says Julia Child Day occurs on the Thursday before Thanksgiving and features Julia Child’s recipes across campus dining halls for dinner.
cards.access_notes: Campus dining access and menu details are determined by Smith for the annual observance.

cards.title: Spot seniors’ creative hats and first regalia
cards.subtitle: Annual all-college convocation
cards.notes: Follow the annual convocation announcement and look for seniors wearing graduation robes for the first time, often with creative hats.
cards.short_summary: A February gathering with Smith College Medals and senior regalia.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith calls Rally Day an annual tradition where distinguished alums receive Smith College Medals and seniors first wear graduation regalia, often with creative hats.
cards.access_notes: Smith schedules Rally Day annually in February; consult the current event page for attendance details.

cards.title: See the graduating class plant ceremonial ivy
cards.subtitle: Day-before-Commencement procession
cards.notes: During Commencement Weekend, watch the senior procession and ceremonial ivy planting that symbolizes graduates’ connection to Smith.
cards.short_summary: A century-plus commencement rite rooted in the Class of 1884.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith states that Ivy Day has been a tradition for more than a century; the Class of 1884 first planted ivy as part of its graduation ceremonies.
cards.source_title: Commencement & Ivy Day Traditions | Smith College
cards.access_notes: Held on the day before Commencement as part of Smith’s graduation weekend.

cards.title: See the campus glow with colored lanterns
cards.subtitle: Commencement Weekend evening tradition
cards.notes: Return at dusk during Commencement Weekend to view colored paper lanterns and major-building light displays across campus.
cards.short_summary: A lantern-lit evening for graduating students to reflect together.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith says Illumination Night lights the campus with colored paper lanterns and fanciful light displays on some major buildings.
cards.source_title: Commencement & Ivy Day Traditions | Smith College
cards.access_notes: Occurs during Commencement Weekend; confirm the current weekend program before visiting.

cards.title: Watch reunion classes parade in white
cards.subtitle: Ivy Day procession tradition
cards.notes: During reunion weekend, look for alumnae classes in white, differentiated by colored ribbons and carrying class placards in the parade.
cards.short_summary: A reunion procession first officially held in 1909.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith says the first official Alumnae Parade was held in 1909; alumnae now dress in white, use colored ribbons for reunion classes and carry placards.
cards.source_title: Commencement & Ivy Day Traditions | Smith College
cards.access_notes: The parade is part of Smith’s Reunion and Ivy Day programming; check that year’s schedule.

cards.title: Notice the laurel chain leading the seniors
cards.subtitle: Carried by Junior Ushers on Ivy Day
cards.notes: Watch the Ivy Day procession for Junior Ushers carrying the shoulder-borne chain, which Smith notes is actually made of laurel leaves.
cards.short_summary: A deceptively named laurel-leaf procession chain.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith documents an Ivy Day ivy chain carried by Junior Ushers; the chain is made of laurel leaves and precedes the seniors in procession.
cards.source_title: Commencement & Ivy Day Traditions | Smith College
cards.access_notes: Visible within the Ivy Day procession during Commencement Weekend.

cards.title: Watch diplomas travel around the Quad
cards.subtitle: Post-Commencement graduating-class ritual
cards.notes: After Commencement, look toward the Laura Scales/Franklin King terrace as graduates form rings and pass diplomas until each reaches its owner.
cards.short_summary: A post-ceremony circle whose recorded history reaches 1911.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith traces the Diploma Circle to 1911 and says graduates form rings after Commencement, passing diplomas around until each graduate receives the correct one.
cards.source_title: Commencement & Ivy Day Traditions | Smith College
cards.access_notes: Takes place immediately following Smith’s Commencement ceremony.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Smith College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A daylight-to-evening first-weekend route using public campus destinations, a cultural stop, and a current performance option.

cards.title: Start with the campus map
cards.subtitle: Plan your route before setting out
cards.notes: Use the interactive map to search buildings and view accessibility and parking overlays before choosing the next stop.
cards.short_summary: A practical first stop for orienting yourself on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith describes its interactive map as an accessible wayfinding guide with building details and parking and accessibility overlays.
cards.access_notes: Use the map’s accessibility overlay to plan an appropriate route.

cards.title: Take a pond-side orientation walk
cards.subtitle: College Lane and Paradise Pond
cards.notes: Walk beside Paradise Pond to get your bearings; the college identifies it as a campus attraction and science learning site.
cards.short_summary: A scenic campus landmark near the main entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith says Paradise Pond, formed by a Mill River dam in the 18th century, is a campus attraction and living laboratory for science students.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor destination; check conditions and follow posted campus guidance.

cards.title: Step into Lyman Plant House
cards.subtitle: Botanic Garden of Smith College, 16 College Lane
cards.notes: Visit the conservatory’s plant collections and exhibits, then pick up an accessible-route map at the front desk if needed.
cards.short_summary: An indoor garden stop with year-round public access.
cards.evidence_claim: The Botanic Garden says Lyman Plant House & Conservatory is free and open to the public, normally daily from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
cards.source_title: Visit | Botanic Garden of Smith College
cards.access_notes: Normally open daily 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; closed during winter break and hours change for the annual flower show.

cards.title: Continue through the Arboretum
cards.subtitle: Botanic Garden of Smith College grounds
cards.notes: Make this the outdoor counterpart to the conservatory: follow the garden paths and pause at plants or exhibits that catch your eye.
cards.short_summary: A self-paced walk through Smith’s outdoor botanical collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith’s Botanic Garden says its campus arboretum and gardens are open daily to the public year-round.
cards.source_title: Visit | Botanic Garden of Smith College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor gardens are open daily year-round; groups of 10 or more should schedule in advance.

cards.title: Browse the museum galleries
cards.subtitle: 20 Elm Street at Bedford Terrace
cards.notes: Choose one gallery or exhibition to explore rather than trying to cover everything, and check the museum page before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A free art stop in the Brown Fine Arts Center.
cards.evidence_claim: SCMA lists free admission and public museum hours Tuesday through Sunday, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m.
cards.source_title: Visit | Smith College Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Tuesday–Sunday, 11 a.m.–4 p.m.; closed Mondays and major holidays.

cards.title: Settle into Neilson Library
cards.subtitle: Smith College Libraries
cards.notes: Use the floor-by-floor guide to find a suitable reading or browsing area, and check the live occupancy display before claiming a seat.
cards.short_summary: A library stop for browsing, reading, or a quiet reset.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith Libraries provides a floor-by-floor guide, real-time occupancy information, and current hours for Neilson Library.
cards.access_notes: Consult the library’s current-hours table and entry guidance before visiting.

cards.title: Meet up at the Campus Center
cards.subtitle: 100 Elm Street, beside Chapin Lawn
cards.notes: Use the Campus Center as a low-key meetup point, then step outside to Chapin Lawn for a change of scene.
cards.short_summary: A central campus gathering place with access to Chapin Lawn.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith says the Campus Center opens onto Chapin Lawn and is open to Smith community members and guests seeking a place to relax.
cards.source_title: Office of Student Engagement | Smith College
cards.access_notes: Guests are included in Smith’s stated Campus Center access; follow facility policies and any posted event restrictions.

cards.title: Pause on Chapin Lawn
cards.subtitle: Outside the Smith College Campus Center
cards.notes: Take a daylight break on the lawn directly outside the Campus Center, then use the map to choose an evening venue nearby.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor pause built into the center of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith’s Office of Student Engagement states that the Campus Center opens out onto Chapin Lawn.
cards.source_title: Office of Student Engagement | Smith College
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access may be affected by weather or scheduled campus use.

cards.entity_name: Smith College Music Event at Sage Hall
cards.title: Check the music calendar
cards.subtitle: Sage Hall: Sweeney Concert Hall or Earle Recital Hall
cards.notes: If a music event fits your weekend, confirm its time and venue on SmithArts; Smith lists music events as free and unticketed.
cards.short_summary: A no-ticket option for adding a campus performance to the weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: SmithArts states that all Music Department events are free and open to the public, with no tickets or reservations required.
cards.source_title: Attend an Event | Smith College Performing Arts
cards.access_notes: Confirm the specific event on the performance calendar; the cited page lists Sage Hall music venues.

cards.title: End with a Theatre 14 performance
cards.subtitle: Mendenhall Center for the Performing Arts, 122 Green Street
cards.notes: For a theatre or dance evening, check the current season and buy a ticket only if a listed performance fits your schedule.
cards.short_summary: A named SmithArts venue for scheduled theatre and dance performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Smith identifies Theatre 14 in Mendenhall Center as a 460-seat proscenium venue and directs visitors to purchase theatre and dance tickets through SmithArts.
cards.source_title: Attend an Event | Smith College Performing Arts
cards.access_notes: Theatre and dance performances use SmithArts ticketing; confirm the current calendar, ticket availability, and accessibility needs before attending.
